column2: A four-wheeled robot you can talk to, drive from a web panel on your phone or from Telegram, that sees through a camera, plays music and radio, follows the object in front of it, and keeps watch. Built step by step from the battery to the AI, with a small test at every step.
The robot has been fully assembled and tested on real hardware: driving and the safety stop, sensors, head, touch screen, two-way voice, camera, music and radio, Telegram, the web panel, and the AI.
The three full sketches and 17 test sketches are written for the Arduino ESP32 core 3.3.12.
Pins were chosen to avoid the boot, PSRAM, and USB pins on both ESP32s, and every module's voltage was checked against its datasheet.

Screen and SD card: both share the long SPI wires on the breadboard. The symptoms are a white screen or an SD card that is not read. The fixes are in the "if it fails" part of Part 3 Steps 2 and 3: lower LAYAR_MHZ, turn off all power including USB and turn it back on, and add a capacitor on the 3.3 V rail.
The TB6612 and screen pin order differ between sellers. Match the pin names printed on the board when wiring.
The robot's voice uses an unofficial Google TTS service that can stop at any time. Free AI quotas can change at any time.
Made for learning. The complete robot has been assembled and tested on real hardware.
The complete robot has been assembled and tested on real hardware. Unplug power before changing wires.

Plain white screen: RESET, DC, or CS is not connected, or SCK/MOSI are swapped. If the wiring is right but it stays white (or is sometimes white when the switch is turned on), the long jumper wires cannot keep up at 27 MHz: in robot_otak set #define LAYAR_MHZ 20 (or 10), in the test sketch lower freq_write to 20000000. The robot_otak Serial Monitor also prints [layar] lines: if "chip sentuh menjawab ... HIDUP" appears but the screen is white, the problem is in the screen's own wires (SCK, SDI, CS, DC, RESET), not the module power.

Sometimes read, sometimes not, even though the wires beep in the continuity test: turn on Tools → Core Debug Level → Error. If Card Failed! cmd: 0x37 or 0x29 appears, the wires are fine but the card will not get ready. The RST button and uploading do not cut power to the card, so unplug USB and turn the switch off for 10 seconds, then turn it back on. Add a 100-470 µF electrolytic capacitor on the 3.3 V rail near the screen module (+ leg to the red rail), because the card draws a large current when it starts. If it still fails, reformat with SD Card Formatter (FAT32) or replace the card.

Song stops midway or the screen flickers while a song plays from SD: SD reading is being disturbed. robot_otak already uses 10 MHz and resumes the song by itself if the SD stalls; a capacitor on the 3.3 V rail also helps.
